editorial:
Imagine you are running from the mob with a huge debt over your head and nowhere to hide. That is exactly where you find yourself as the main character, a smooth-talking con artist who decides to crash at a fancy house in the suburbs. By pretending to be an old family friend, you get a free place to stay and a chance to dodge the bad guys. The vibe is light and silly, making it a great pick for a lazy Sunday afternoon when you just want to laugh at someone else's chaotic life.

The acting is the best part here, as the lead does a great job playing a guy who is always one step away from getting caught. The pacing moves quickly, though some of the jokes feel a bit dated since it is from the 90s. Still, it is a fun ride that keeps you guessing if the family will find out the truth.
endingExplained: In the end, the con man finally stops lying and shows his true colors. The mobsters catch up to him, but through a series of funny accidents and some help from the family, he manages to outsmart them. He pays back what he owes and learns that being honest is actually easier than lying. He leaves the house on good terms, having actually made some real friends along the way.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves lighthearted comedies about scams and family chaos.
